# PR type
- [ ] Bug Fix
- [ ] New Feature
- [ ] Document Updates
- [ ] More Models or Datasets Support
- [x] Optimization

## Summary

This PR vectorizes `get_half_index` for packed multi-document sequence-parallel ring attention.

The previous implementation created a CPU boolean mask and iterated over every document boundary in Python. This caused repeated host-side scalar reads when `cu_seqlens` was on NPU.

This change:

- Keeps the existing `slice` fast path for a single document.
- Builds a device-resident `torch.long` gather index for multiple documents.
- Preserves odd-length document behavior.
- Preserves the existing `ctx.is_half_index_tensor` contract.
- Removes per-document host synchronization.

## Experiment results

NPU microbenchmark results with fixed total token count. Values are synchronized median/p95 latency in microseconds; speedup is computed from median latency:

| Packed documents | Baseline median/p95 | Optimized median/p95 | Median speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 239.1 / 304.7 | 234.5 / 246.0 | 1.02x |
| 2 | 918.5 / 939.1 | 897.1 / 922.6 | 1.02x |
| 4 | 1467.8 / 1520.9 | 892.4 / 922.3 | 1.64x |
| 8 | 2496.1 / 3004.0 | 890.9 / 925.8 | 2.80x |
| 32 | 8734.3 / 8827.5 | 899.0 / 923.6 | 9.72x |
| 128 | 33478.1 / 34246.6 | 923.8 / 944.8 | 36.24x |
| 512 | 132836.8 / 141790.6 | 1006.3 / 1022.6 | 132.00x |
| 1024 | 252684.0 / 257457.1 | 1136.3 / 1169.7 | 222.36x |

The benchmark follows the repository NPU benchmark convention: 10 warmup iterations, 30 synchronized measurement iterations, and median/p95 reporting.

The small-document regression is below the 10% threshold, so no additional scalar fallback was added.

Training smoke test on 8 Ascend 910B3 NPUs:

- `sequence_parallel_size=8`
- `sp_world_size=2`
- `rp_world_size=4`
- `padding_free=true`
- Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with LoRA

Results:

```text
baseline runtime:   22.49s
optimized runtime:  19.26s
```

The optimized implementation was exercised by the real ring-attention training path. Outputs, gradients, and training loss matched the baseline.

## Validation

Passed:

```text
CPU tests:                 73 passed, 6 skipped
Sequence-parallel tests:   95 passed, 7 skipped
NPU parity tests:          28 configurations passed
Distributed E2E:            2-rank and 8-rank numerical equivalence
Pre-commit:                 all configured hooks passed
```

The changed files are:

```text
swift/sequence_parallel/zigzag_ring_attn.py
tests/sequence_parallel/test_zigzag_ring_attn.py
tests/sequence_parallel/test_zigzag_ring_attn_npu.py
```

The repository-style NPU benchmark is opt-in and can be run with:

```bash
SWIFT_RUN_NPU_BENCHMARK=1 \
python -m pytest -s \
  tests/sequence_parallel/test_zigzag_ring_attn_npu.py \
  -k get_half_index_benchmark
```

It uses 10 warmup iterations, 30 synchronized measurement iterations, and reports median/p95 latency. CUDA was not available in the current validation environment, so CUDA-specific runtime validation and benchmarking are not included in this PR. If this implementation is considered solid based on the NPU results and CI validation, GPU-specific validation or follow-up optimization can be handled in a separate PR.

# Checklist

- [x] I have linked the related issue above, if there is one.
- [x] I have reviewed and understand every changed line, and I can explain how the change works and why it is correct.
- [x] I have run the relevant tests and pre-commit checks locally.
- [x] I am responsible for the content of this PR, regardless of how it was produced.

@@ -18,7 +18,7 @@ def get_half_index(cu_seqlens, *, front: bool):
         front: The head part or the tail part
 
     Returns:
-        The slice or the tensor mask.
+        The slice, or a 1-D index tensor on ``cu_seqlens.device``.
     """
 
     if len(cu_seqlens) == 2:
@@ -27,15 +27,25 @@ def get_half_index(cu_seqlens, *, front: bool):
         else:
             return slice(cu_seqlens[-1] // 2, None)
 
-    index = torch.zeros((cu_seqlens[-1].item(), ), dtype=torch.bool)
-    for i in range(len(cu_seqlens) - 1):
-        start, end = cu_seqlens[i], cu_seqlens[i + 1]
-        if front:
-            end = (start + end) // 2
-        else:
-            start = (start + end) // 2
-        index[start:end] = True
-    return index
+    # Build the gather index on device in one shot. A per-document loop reads
+    # every boundary back to the host, and a bool mask would additionally make
+    # each consumer run `nonzero()`; both serialize the device queue.
+    cu_seqlens = cu_seqlens.to(dtype=torch.long)
+    lengths = cu_seqlens[1:] - cu_seqlens[:-1]
+    front_lengths = lengths // 2
+    if front:
+        counts = front_lengths
+        source_starts = cu_seqlens[:-1]
+    else:
+        # Keep the tail of an odd length longer, as `start = (start + end) // 2` did.
+        counts = lengths - front_lengths
+        source_starts = cu_seqlens[:-1] + front_lengths
+    # The only host readback left, and it is independent of the document count.
+    total_len = int(counts.sum())
+    destination_starts = torch.cumsum(counts, dim=0) - counts
+    source_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(source_starts, counts, output_size=total_len)
+    destination_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(destination_starts, counts, output_size=total_len)
+    return source_indices + torch.arange(total_len, device=cu_seqlens.device) - destination_indices

+def _reference_get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front):
+    """The original per-document bool-mask implementation, kept as the oracle."""
+    index = torch.zeros((cu_seqlens[-1].item(), ), dtype=torch.bool)

+            end = (start + end) // 2
+        else:
+            start = (start + end) // 2
+        index[start:end] = True

+
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize('cu_dtype', (torch.int32, torch.int64))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('front', (True, False))
+def test_get_half_index_gather_matches_reference(lengths, cu_dtype, front):
+    cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens(lengths, dtype=cu_dtype)
+    source = torch.randn((sum(lengths), 2, 4))
+
+    index = get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=front)
+    reference = _reference_get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(source[index], source[reference], rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('front', (True, False))
+def test_get_half_index_accumulation_matches_reference(front):
+    lengths = [2, 4, 6, 8, 2, 4, 6, 8, 2]
+    cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens(lengths, dtype=torch.int64)
+
+    index = get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=front)
+    reference = _reference_get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front)
+    gradient = torch.randn((sum(lengths) // 2, 2, 4))
+
+    actual = torch.zeros((sum(lengths), 2, 4))
+    expected = torch.zeros_like(actual)
+    actual[index] += gradient
+    expected[reference] += gradient
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_get_half_index_halves_are_complementary():
+    lengths = [2, 4, 6, 8, 2, 4, 6, 8, 2]
+    cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens(lengths, dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    front_index = get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=True)
+    tail_index = get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=False)
+    covered = torch.cat((front_index, tail_index)).sort().values
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(covered, torch.arange(sum(lengths)), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_get_half_index_returns_slice_for_a_single_sequence():
+    cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens([8], dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    # The autograd function branches on this type via `ctx.is_half_index_tensor`.
+    assert isinstance(get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=True), slice)
+    assert isinstance(get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=False), slice)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('cu_dtype', (torch.int32, torch.int64))
+def test_get_half_index_is_built_on_the_input_device(cu_dtype):
+    cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens([2, 4, 6, 8], dtype=cu_dtype)
+
+    index = get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=False)
+
+    assert index.device == cu_seqlens.device
+    assert index.dtype == torch.long
+
+
+def test_get_half_index_host_readbacks_do_not_grow_with_document_count(monkeypatch):
+    original = {
+        'item': torch.Tensor.item,
+        'int': torch.Tensor.__int__,
+        'index': torch.Tensor.__index__,
+    }
+    counts = {}
+
+    def make_counter(name):
+
+        def counter(self):
+            counts[name] += 1
+            return original[name](self)
+
+        return counter
+
+    for name in original:
+        monkeypatch.setattr(torch.Tensor, f'__{name}__' if name != 'item' else 'item', make_counter(name))
+
+    readbacks = {}
+    for num_documents in (4, 128):
+        cu_seqlens = _make_cu_seqlens([8] * num_documents, dtype=torch.int32)
+        counts.update({name: 0 for name in original})
+        get_half_index(cu_seqlens, front=False)
+        readbacks[num_documents] = sum(counts.values())
+
+    # The old loop read two boundaries per document; only a single length readback is left.
+    assert readbacks[4] == readbacks[128]
+    assert readbacks[128] <= 1

+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    assert index.device == cu_seqlens.device
+    torch.testing.assert_close(source[index], source[reference], rtol=0, atol=0)
